messages.subject: Repeated Measures (Within Subjects Designs)
parts:
Hello list.
I'm trying to better understand repeated measures model but i got a
little stuck trying to make an Repeated Measures (Within Subjects
Designs) model on openbugs.
Hope i'm not falling to far from the list topics.

Suppose i have the following data:
#The data, measures collected along 4 times (tempo) on 60 subjects
(id) on a 3 level treatment (trat), the response variable is the
medidas:
dados<-data.frame(tempo=factor(rep(c(0,1,2,3),each=60)),

trat=factor(rep(rep(c("controle","dose1","dose2"),each=20),4)),
id=factor(rep(1:60,4)),medidas=0)
str(dados)
dados[dados$tempo==0,"medidas"]<-rnorm(60,rep(c(5,5,5),each=20),1)
dados[dados$tempo==1,"medidas"]<-dados[dados$tempo==0,"medidas"]+rep(c(0,0,0),each=20)+rnorm(60,0,1)
dados[dados$tempo==2,"medidas"]<-dados[dados$tempo==1,"medidas"]+rep(c(0,0,0),each=20)+rnorm(60,0,1)
dados[dados$tempo==3,"medidas"]<-dados[dados$tempo==2,"medidas"]+rep(c(0,0,2),each=20)+rnorm(60,0,1)

#So all measures start the same, and only for dose2 on the tempo 2 to
3 it increase
with(dados, interaction.plot(tempo,trat,medidas, lwd = 3,
ylab = "Medidas", xlab = "tempo", trace.label = "trat"))

#So tempo, trat and the interaction is important.
summary(aov(medidas~trat*tempo+Error(id),data=dados))

#And we can estimate the parameters like this, with nlme
library(nlme)
modelo.ar1 <- gls(medidas~trat*tempo-1,data=dados,corr=corAR1(,form=~1|id))
summary(modelo.ar1)

Now i cant figure out how to estimate parameters with Bayesian
framework, using OpenBugs.
I suppose i need something like this:

model {
for ( i in 1:N ) {
y[i] ~ dnorm( mu[i] , tau )
mu[i] <- trat[x1[i]] + temp[x2[i]] + trattemp[x1[i],x2[i]]+Subject[id[i]]
}

But i cant figure out how to put the Correlation matrix on the model,
nor how determine a naive priors. If someone know more examples of
model definition for within subjects that cover this topic, it would
be great.

I'm trying to adapt some other models, there is a poisson model on
openbugs examples page (http://www.openbugs.info/Examples/Epil.html)
and one totally different way on the book Doing Bayesian Analysis
(http://www.indiana.edu/%7Ekruschke/DoingBayesianDataAnalysis/Programs/ProgramsDoingBayesianDataAnalysis.zip
, ANOVAtwowayBRugsWithinSubj.R file )

On the openbugs it seem to me that every measure is right subtracted
from the common mean and for Doing Bayesian Analysis it is subtracted
outside.

Well i'm really stuck try to put things to work, so if someone could
enlight my way :)

Thanks for the attention and patience on reading.

Best wishes
